title: Marketing calendar — a record of every month that was planned
note: Filed by `lab/the owner/marketing-calendar/machine/records.py` after a run of the nine-layer calendar flow. One record per planned month per brand; the item id is the run label (`calendar-2026-09`, `calendar-2026-09-Brand B`), so several records exist for one month and the LATEST BY `at` WINS — a re-plan is a new record, never an edit of the old one. POINTERS, NEVER CONTENT: nothing here carries a slot, an angle or a line of copy. The month itself lives in the run folder the record names, and the reviewer's own judgements live in `review.json` beside it; this plane carries counts and state so the dashboard can show which months exist, which are clean, and which a human has finished with. The `review` block is the whole point of the kind — a month that planned cleanly and that nobody has read is not a month that is ready to send, and those are two different facts that the counts keep apart.

verdict_fields.note: `plan` is a run of the calendar flow. `review` is a snapshot of where a human got to on a month already planned — filed when the reviewer's decisions change, never on a tick.

`breaks` means the month was produced but its own checker found rules it violates — the month exists and is readable, and is not ready to send. `failed` means the flow did not finish; no slots.json was written.
the brand folder the run read — brand CONTENT only, per rule-9 (brand home)
how many sends the month holds after layer 9 dropped duplicates
rules the month violates, per its own checks.md — the count, never the text
things a human should read but that do not break the month

where the human got to: {pending, approved, needs_work, cut, edited, noted}. `edited` counts slots a reviewer rewrote a field on, `noted` counts slots carrying a note for the writer. Absent on a run nobody has opened.
how many slots have been handed to a writer, by state: {queued, running, done, failed}. The hand-off command itself is named in the component's handoff.json, never here.
wall-clock of the whole flow, when the run recorded one

All NINE layers, in chain order, keyed by the chain's own keys (declared in lab/the owner/marketing-calendar/machine/chain.py). Per layer: n, by (code|ai), status, produced, seconds — and for the two thinking layers the prompt file name and its sha. the owner's standing rule is that the prompt is the product, so the version that decided a month is part of that month's record. `status` is `done` (ran), `carried` (a replay reused this layer's output from disk and carried its record forward), or `unrecorded` (reused from disk with no prior record, so the prompt behind it cannot be named). The list is always complete: a layer missing from the record and a layer that did not run must never look the same.

The layers whose output governs this month but whose run was never recorded — a NAMED hole. Absent (null) on a month planned end to end. Non-empty means the month is not fully reproducible: re-plan it if that matters, or accept it knowingly.

where the month lives — a POINTER. The engine writes everywhere under its `--out`, so this is wherever the caller sent it; a reader opens board.html there and never reconstructs a month from this record.
the review page inside the run folder, relative to it
